root.name: French Defense: Henneberger Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Be3

overview: White develops 4.Be3 instead of the usual Bg5, Bd3 or e5, supporting d4 and keeping the options of Qd2 and long castling. Black can strike with ...dxe4, ...Bb4 or ...Bd6. It is a quiet, flexible line.

white_ideas.idea: Qd2 and long castling with a kingside pawn push
Support d4 and the e4 centre

typical_structures.structure: French with White e4/d4 chain and Black e6/d5

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Fully respectable but gives Black easy equality.

structure.notes: Black can resolve the centre with ...dxe4 for a semi-open position.

approach.notes: A less common choice that is nonetheless played by strong players.

character.reason: A flexible, quiet development rather than a forcing line.

structure.reason: Black often trades with ...dxe4 for a French semi-open position.

approach.reason: Less common but not seldom chosen by strong players.

plans.reason: White keeps a space edge in the centre.
